Finding a Room to Rent

Ask for information, understand numbers, dates and spelling, and complete a form while you listen — the core of IELTS Listening Part 1.

Level: A1–A2 → A2
Exam focus: Listening Parts 1–2
Mock: 20 questions · 20 min
Class: 60 minutes
1
Warm-up

Your first home in the UK

5 min

Rafael is from Brazil. He is moving to Leeds for a job. First, he needs a room. Read this advert.

RoomFinderRooms to rent › Leeds › Headingley · Ad 48213
Bills included1 / 6 photos
Double room · Headingley, Leeds LS6
Double room in a friendly shared house
£575 pcm(£133 pw) · all bills included
FurnishedShared kitchen & bathroomFibre Wi-Fi5 min to bus stop
Available
1 November
Deposit
£663 (5 weeks' rent)
Household
3 professionals + live-in landlord
Rules
Professionals only · No pets · No smokers
Posted 2 days agoCall Tom · 0113 496 0721
Task 1

Read the advert. Choose the answer.

  1. How much is the rent each month?
  2. Are the bills included?
  3. When can you move in?
  4. Can you live there with a cat?
  5. Is the house near public transport?
UK

pcm = per calendar month · pw = per week (£133 pw × 52 ÷ 12 ≈ £575 pcm).

In England, a tenant's deposit can be 5 weeks' rent at most, and the landlord must protect it in a government deposit scheme. Since 1 May 2026 (the Renters' Rights Act), landlords can ask for only one month's rent in advance, and tenants can ask to keep a pet — the landlord needs a good reason to say no.

This room has a live-in landlord, so Rafael would be a lodger. Lodgers have fewer rights: for example, deposit protection and the new pet rules do not apply.

Talk to your teacher: Do you like this room? What is important for you in a new home — price, location, internet, quiet? (Answer with: For me, … is important because …)
2
Grammar

Asking for information

12 min

A · Question words

In IELTS Listening Part 1, one person usually asks questions and the other person gives information. If you know the question word, you know what kind of answer is coming.

Question wordIt asks about…Example
Whata thing, informationWhat's your name? What's the address?
Wherea placeWhere is the house?
Whena day or a dateWhen does your job start?
What timea timeWhat time is the viewing?
How mucha price, moneyHow much is the rent?
How manya number of thingsHow many people live in the house?
Whoa personWho is the landlord?
How do you spell…?lettersHow do you spell your surname?

Questions with be

Is the room furnished? → Yes, it is.
Are the bills included? → No, they aren't.
Is there a washing machine? → Yes, there is.
Are there any shops near the house? → Yes, there are.

!

Singular → is. Plural → are.
the room is · the rooms are
the rent is · the bills are

B · Numbers, dates, times and spelling

About half of the answers in Listening Part 1 are numbers, dates, times or names that are spelled. Learn how British people say them. Press 🔈 to listen; press again to stop.

Phone numbers

07946 352118

"oh-seven-nine-four-six · three-five-two · one-one-eight"
0 = "oh" · 11 = "double one"

Prices

£650 pcm

"six hundred and fifty pounds a month"
In the test, write the number: 650

Dates

3 November

"the third of November"
1st first · 2nd second · 3rd third · 4th fourth · 22nd twenty-second

Times

10.30 · 4.15 · 4.45

"half past ten" · "quarter past four" · "quarter to five"

3
Vocabulary + life skill

Words for renting a home

10 min

Study the 12 words. Press 🔈 to hear each word and the example sentence.

flatnoun
A home on one floor of a building. (US: apartment)
I live in a small flat.
shared housenoun
A house where people who are not a family live. Everyone has a room.
I live with three housemates.
landlord / landladynoun
The person who owns the home and gets the rent.
The landlord fixes problems.
tenantnoun
The person who rents and lives in the home.
Tenants pay rent every month.
letting agentnoun
A company that finds tenants for landlords.
Brightway Lettings is a letting agent.
rentnoun / verb
Money you pay every month to live in a home.
The rent is £575 pcm.
depositnoun
Money you pay before you move in. You get it back at the end if there is no damage.
The deposit is 5 weeks' rent.
billsnoun, plural
Money for gas, electricity, water and internet.
Bills are included.
furnishedadjective
With furniture: a bed, a desk, a sofa. Opposite: unfurnished.
The room is furnished.
viewingnoun
A visit to see a home before you rent it.
Can I book a viewing?
tenancy agreementnoun
The contract between the landlord and the tenant.
Read it before you sign.
council taxnoun
Money for the local council (bins, roads, libraries).
Is council tax included?
+

Also useful: housemate (a person you share a house with) · studio (one room with a kitchen and bathroom) · en-suite (a bedroom with its own bathroom).

4
Exam strategy

How to complete a form while you listen

8 min
1

Read the instructions

In the real test you type the answer. The usual limit is ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER.

2

Predict the answer

Is it a name? a number? a date? a time? a place? Use the time before the recording.

3

Listen for changes

People change their minds: "Oh no, sorry…", "I was thinking… but…". The last answer is usually correct.

4

Check spelling

A wrong spelling is a wrong answer. Check plurals: bill or bills?

The word limit: ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER

You write…OK?
Saturday✓ one word
10.30✓ a number
14 Hyde✓ word + number
on Saturday✗ two words
half past ten✗ three words

Exercise 7

Distractor detective — what is the final answer?

IELTS often says a wrong answer first. Read and choose the answer you should write.

  1. "Can I come on Thursday? Oh no, wait — Thursday I'm working. Is Friday OK?"
  2. "The rent was £600 last year, but now it's £625."
  3. "My number is 07700 900418 — sorry, it's 481 at the end."
  4. "I thought about a studio, but a room in a shared house is cheaper, so that's what I want."

  5. There are 20 questions. Each question is worth 1 mark.

Teacher notes — lesson timing

00–05 Advert + Task 1. Elicit: pcm, bills, deposit.
05–17 Question words, Ex 1–2. Numbers and alphabet; drill the 7 sound groups. Ex 3.
17–27 Vocabulary cards (pronunciation), Ex 4–5.
27–35 4-step strategy, word-limit table, Ex 6–8.
35–55 Mock exam, exam conditions.
55–60 Check answers with the transcript; set homework.
!

Watch for: letters E/I and G/J; "fifteen/fifty"; the date the speaker corrects. In the real test, Part 1 answers are typed (or written on paper) and spelling counts. The mock lets students type, or choose from a list if they are not ready yet — practise spelling out loud in the homework.

Homework (about 45 minutes)

  1. Listen again to the mock in the Transcript tab. Find each answer and the wrong answer before it. (15 min)
  2. Spell out loud and record: your full name, your street, your future employer's name, your email address. (10 min)
  3. Learn the 12 words plus housemate, studio, en-suite. Say one sentence about your own home with each. (10 min)
  4. Real UK life: find two real room adverts in Leeds, Manchester or London. For each, note: rent · bills? · deposit · nearest transport. (10 min)
